question: How does the length of the alkyl tail on imidazolium cations influence density turnover and nanostructuring in ionic liquid and water binary mixtures?
answer: The length of the alkyl tail on imidazolium cations significantly influences density turnover and nanostructuring in ionic liquid (IL)/water binary mixtures. For shorter-tailed [emim][Ac], density peaks at a water mole fraction (Xw) of 0.5 due to maximal polar domain structuring (cation headgroups, anions, and water), followed by a decline as further water disrupts hydrogen-bonded anion bridges. In contrast, longer-tailed [bmim][Ac] and [hmim][Ac] delay density turnover to Xw > 0.7 because water-induced tail aggregation sustains nanostructuring. The initial density rise stems from water-mediated anion bridging, while the turnover occurs when bifurcated water-anion bonds weaken polar domain correlations. Thus, alkyl tail length dictates the water concentration at which density turnover occurs by modulating tail aggregation and polar domain stability.

The purpose of the paper is to investigate the unusual density behavior of 1-alkyl-3-methyl imidazolium acetate ([Rₙmim][Ac]) ionic liquid (IL) and water binary mixtures at low to moderate water concentrations. Using molecular dynamics simulations, the study aims to uncover the molecular mechanisms underlying the density increase and turnover by examining nanostructural reordering and spatial correlations. The findings are intended to provide insights for optimizing IL/water mixtures for biochemical applications.
